item.title: Urban Distribution Reliability Upgrade with Smart Monitoring
item.description:
Project Background

A dense urban district faced repeated customer complaints during summer peaks. Existing equipment lacked real-time visibility, making fault isolation and maintenance scheduling slow.

Solution

The utility launched a staged retrofit program centered on transformer modernization:

  • Deployed higher-efficiency distribution transformers at overloaded nodes.
  • Added online monitoring for winding temperature, load rate, and alarms.
  • Established data-driven maintenance triggers instead of fixed interval inspection.

Results

Within the first maintenance cycle, the utility achieved:

item.title: Oil-Immersed Transformer for a Utility-Scale Solar Project
item.description:
Project Background

A 120 MW photovoltaic project required robust step-up transformation across multiple inverter blocks. The owner needed high thermal endurance, low no-load loss, and reliable operation in hot, dusty conditions.

Solution

The EPC selected sealed oil-immersed transformers with corrosion-resistant outdoor configuration:

  • Optimized impedance matching for inverter output characteristics.
  • Adopted on-load monitoring for oil temperature and load profile.
  • Implemented phased commissioning to shorten grid-connection risk windows.

Results

After the first operating season, the project team observed:

item.title: Dry-Type Transformer Upgrade for an Electronics Plant
item.description:
Project Background

A large electronics manufacturing site had recurring line trips during peak shifts. The existing transformers had high heat rise and unstable voltage under variable-frequency motor loads, causing process interruptions and scrap risk.

Solution

The customer adopted new SCB-series dry-type transformers near key production zones and rebalanced feeder allocation:

  • Replaced legacy units with low-loss, low-noise dry-type models.
  • Added temperature monitoring and alarm integration to the plant BMS.
  • Reconfigured cable routing to reduce distribution distance and voltage drop.

Results

Within three months of commissioning, the plant reported:
